svg.title: Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy Energy Landscapes: Uniaxial vs Cubic Conventions
svg.desc: Two-panel comparison of Fullmag's magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy densities: (a) uniaxial energy polar surfaces (easy axis, easy plane, and easy cone) and explicit constant energy offset against the sin^2(theta) convention while keeping H_u identical, and (b) 3D cubic anisotropy energy surfaces and (1-10)-plane profiles for Kc1 > 0 (<100> easy) and Kc1 < 0 (<111> easy).
svg.text: Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy Landscapes: Uniaxial and Cubic Conventions
Exact Fullmag negative-power uniaxial form −Ku1q² − Ku2q⁴ (with offset vs sin²θ) and cubic crystal-frame polynomial
Uniaxial Anisotropy: wu = −Ku1 q² − Ku2 q⁴
q = m·û = cos θ; easy axis, easy plane, easy cone, and sin²θ offset
Easy axis (Ku1 > 0, Ku2 = 0): min at θ = 0°, 180°
Easy plane (Ku1 < 0, Ku2 = 0): min at θ = 90°
No Poisson solve; no boundary condition of its own.
Absolute Scalar Energy Convention Comparison (Ku1 > 0, Ku2 = 0)
Angle θ between m and û [deg]
Conversion vs K'u1 sin²θ + K'u2 sin⁴θ: Ku1 = K'u1 + 2K'u2, Ku2 = −K'u2
Constant energy offset Δw = Ku1 + Ku2; effective field Hu is identical.
Cubic Anisotropy: wc = Kc1 Σ + Kc2 α₁²α₂²α₃² + Kc3 Σ²
Orthonormal crystal frame (ĉ₁, ĉ₂, ĉ₃ = ĉ₁×ĉ₂), αa = m·ĉa, Σ = α₁²α₂² + α₂²α₃² + α₃²α₁²
Crystal-frame rule: FEM strictly requires orthonormal ĉ₁, ĉ₂ (‖ĉa‖ = 1, ĉ₁·ĉ₂ = 0).
FDM normalizes axes and forms ĉ₃ = ĉ₁ × ĉ₂; active axes must stay finite and non-degenerate.
